summary:
Corrientes stands under Argentina's national framework for gender identity, health care, criminal law and document recognition; that national layer is assessed in the Argentina country record and is not restated here.

An April 2025 Washington Blade report, datelined Buenos Aires, names Corrientes among the more conservative interior provinces of Argentina where conditions for trans people are worse than in the capital. The characterisation comes from interviews with trans activists rather than from provincial government data, and the report attaches no Corrientes-specific incident, prosecution or policy to it.

The same reporting records activists' testimony that police violence against trans and travesti sex workers, already common, has increased under the current national government and is worst outside Buenos Aires. Corrientes falls inside the area that testimony describes, but the claim is pitched at the interior as a whole; no provincial police unit, case or complaint from Corrientes is identified.
tangentialFactors:
The only Corrientes-specific signal in the current reporting is comparative: the province is grouped with other interior provinces described as more conservative and worse for trans people than the capital. No provincial statute, provincial court ruling, provincial health directive or provincial police record appears in the sources reviewed.

National measures adopted in 2025 apply in Corrientes as in every other Argentine province. Their content belongs to the Argentina country record and is not repeated here.
localsOnly:
The sources contain no provincial-level information on how Corrientes residents obtain gender-affirming care, change identity documents, or are held in provincial custody. Nothing in the material reviewed describes a provincial health service, civil registry office, prison or police force in Corrientes acting on gender identity.

Residents of Corrientes who need care or documents depend on the national systems set out in the Argentina country record. The sources record no provincial measure that adds to or restricts those systems.
outOfScopeNotes:
The description of Corrientes as one of the more conservative interior provinces rests on activist interviews and is not corroborated by provincial statistics, provincial court records or provincial government statements in the sources reviewed.

No provincial hate-crime count, police complaint figure or prosecution for violence against trans people in Corrientes appears in the sources, and no comparison against the province's general homicide rate can be made from them.

Whether Corrientes has enacted any local anti-discrimination coverage on gender identity, and how provincial authorities have responded to the national measures adopted in 2025, are not established by the sources reviewed.
